messages:
Sam: FYI I prototyped a 'forensic capture' flow in the console: lightweight UI to temporarily force high-fidelity request+response capture for a route to debug hard-to-repro bugs. Wanted quick reactions before filing an RFC.

Nadia: Nice. What controls are you thinking? Who can trigger? Any PII/legal gates? :thinking_face:

Sam: UI idea: 'Start forensic capture' -> short reason -> TTL (5/15/60m) -> optional filter (user_id / trace_id) -> attach ticket link -> submit. Server runs PII/sensitivity classifier and either allows immediate capture or moves to "requires approver" state.

Leo: Ops note: high volume captures can spike ingest. Need per-tenant token cap and global backpressure. Also prefer a cooldown per-route (e.g., 1h) so it's not abused during a canary.

Sam: Agree. Proposal: default per-tenant budget 50k tokens per 60m for forensic captures, per-route cooldown 1h, and a global emergency cutoff that flips captures to sampled metadata-only at 80% load.

Priya: Legal: require mandatory justification and ticket id. If classifier flags PII or sensitive output then require two approvers (engineer + legal). Also insist on restricted raw retention (12h) with auditable access logs. No exports without approvals.

Nadia: UX: show a preview of what would be captured using current redaction rules (sanitized snippet). If preview strips out key fields, show a warning and require explicit confirmation.

Sam: Implementation detail: capture tag header `x-rdw-forensic: <capture-id>` that clients can optionally add to correlate. Ingress sets capture-mode which bypasses sampling but not redaction. Redaction always runs.

DevEx: For developers, show token burn estimate before confirming. Also include a one-click 'create ticket from capture' action after capture ends with links to traces. And include `rollout_tag` so SRE can cancel captures tied to a canary.

Leo: Ingest changes: have capture pipeline honor an ordered fallback: full payload -> p95-only bodies -> headers+metadata only. Each fallback emits an audit event. ops-bot should alert when projected burn >70% for the next 15m.

ops-bot: [sim-alert] Projected forensic token burn for route /v1/completions hits 75% of tenant budget in 9m.

Nadia: Good to have. Question: where do we keep raw vs scrubbed copies and for how long?

Priya: Raw store allowed only short-term, default 12h, encrypted, access via approval ticket. Scrubbed copy allowed long-term in telemetry store with reduced fields. Add retention and access metadata to audit record.

Sam: API sketch:

POST /internal/v1/forensics/captures
{
  "route": "v1/completions",
  "requestor": "sam",
  "ttl_secs": 3600,
  "filter": { "user_id": "u-42" },
  "ticket": "https://zendesk/INC-123",
  "require_double_approve_if_sensitive": true
}

Nadia: Also add `max_tokens_estimate` and `enforce_budget": true` fields. And a `disable_for_prod_tenants` flag for initial rollout.

Priya: Add `customer_consent_provided": true/false`. If false and PII flagged -> block until legal signoff.

DevEx: Console UX: default TTL to lowest, show live token burn, red banner near budget, cancel button, and an audit link. Also supply a developer header suggestion to attach to reproduction runs.

Leo: Rollout plan: internal dev tenants only first, 2-week canary, metrics: token burn, number of approvals, incidents. Provide ops toggles to reduce default budgets per-tenant.

Sam: Small API debate: classifier must run server-side to avoid tampering; console only surfaces classifier outcome. If sensitive -> create "pending-approval" capture record, block capture until approver acts.

Nadia: Agree. We should also require approver role metadata (engineer, legal) in the audit record.

ops-bot: [info] Capture policy fallback matrix saved to /policies/forensic-capture/fallback-v1.

Priya: Legal checklist to include in RFC: classifier threshold, retention times, approver roles, export rules, and incident escalation for any data leak.

DevEx: Add audit export endpoint: GET /internal/v1/forensics/captures/<id>/audit returning justification, approvers, token usage, and links to traces (if allowed). Make it CSV/exportable.

Leo: Also need admin endpoints to revoke/cancel captures globally or per-tenant in emergencies. ops-bot should auto-cancel captures if ingestion crosses emergency threshold.

Sam: I'll draft RFC tomorrow with API, console mockups, ingest fallback, retention & approval rules, rollout plan, and required legal checklist. Will tag infra/sre/legal/devex.

Nadia: +1 pending the RFC details. Make sure the RFC spells out per-tenant defaults and override knobs for SRE.

Leo: +1 (ops wants explicit metrics to monitor).

Priya: +1 pending legal checklist.

DevEx: +1

Sam: Thanks all — will post RFC and prototype link. :rocket:
